articles.title: Asymmetric rhetorical strategies drive partisanship in television news
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Television remains a dominant source of political information in the United States, yet systematic evidence on how partisanship is expressed in televised news remains limited. Prior research has largely treated partisanship as a one-dimensional construct, offering limited insight into the rhetorical strategies that underlie ideological bias. articles.title: Crisis Governance at the Joints. Mapping the Ethical and Societal Territory of Crisis Management Technologies: The Case of Human-Swarm Teaming
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Crisis and disaster governance increasingly relies on technologies that sense, classify and act faster than humans can. Drone swarms coordinated with human operators, known as human-swarm teaming, provide a productive case to review the field of crisis governance. They promise better situational awareness in disaster response, but they also raise questions about human control, responsibility, surveillance, triage, dual use and public legitimacy. articles.title: Whose Safety? Addressing Anti-Blackness in the Age of AI Safety
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: "AI safety" has grown from a niche contingent of actors into the dominant framing for artificial intelligence (AI) assessment and evaluation, overshadowing AI ethics. Through political and monetary influence, AI safety has shifted political focus within the US and abroad. The focus has shifted away from harms that currently affect the public toward threats framed as "existential risks". We argue that safety cannot be achieved while anti-Blackness is left unaddressed. articles.title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
articles.summary: arXiv:2611.24970v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.24979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Programmable logic controllers (PLCs), the industrial computers that operate power and process plants, often run programs whose source code is no longer available; however, every input and output of the controller is logged continuously. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are increasingly embedded in everyday life, transforming how people accomplish tasks and potentially reshaping how they interact with others. articles.summary: arXiv:2611.25269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in knowledge work as an intelligent collaborator to assist in completing tasks. articles.summary: arXiv:2512.23889v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to simulate public opinion, standing in for survey respondents as "silicon samples."
